::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 26th 1899  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS  West Sussex County Record Office/ Add. 16,944/4
:::

Dear [Miss Walker](people/person_2234.qmd)
I was much interested in your letter, though I am afraid I had not heard [Miss Lawrence](people/person_2199.qmd)’s name.  I believe my [mother](people/person_1606.qmd)left school at 14 in consequence of her[father](people/person_106.qmd)’s very sudden death, so her career there must have been a short one.  I have always thought it must have been a very good school, her knowledge was so thorough, and she taught me almost entirely except a French master and arithmetic, mathematics and Latin from my [father](people/person_1631.qmd). What you tell me of my dear early friend [Mary Davys](people/person_1201.qmd) is most interesting, and just like her.  She had not rank enough to be a Maid of honour, though she lived with them and her right designation was Resident Bedchamber Woman.  Her chief work was to receive the Ministers while they were waiting for the [Queen](people/person_1694.qmd).  She made us one long visit in her holidays, and once we went to see her in Buckingham palace.  She married [Mr Pratt](people/person_1200.qmd), but I only saw her once afterwards,  I always heard of him as very excellent but also that the old clergyman in ‘[Miss Toosey](other_books/otherbook_746.qmd) was a likeness. They had four daughters, two of whom poor things were burnt to death from muslin dresses taking fire from bedcandles.[^1]  I saw much more latterly of [Julia](people/person_57.qmd), whose [husband](people/person_58.qmd) became Dean of Peterborough.  She only died last year.  Her daughter’s husband Mr Rawnsley had the Duke of Albany and the Battenburg boys at his school in the New Forest.[^2] I do wonder that I should not have heard of Miss Lawrence, but I think the languor always consequent of being in London must have hung upon the recollection of schoolfellows

Petty scandal and ‘Airs and Graces’ always seem to me wondrously clever  I wonder if the Black Lane still exists[^3]

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The four daughters were [Florence Maria](people/person_1203.qmd), [Fanny Mary Harriet](people/person_1202.qmd), [Ethel Julia](people/person_1204.qmd) and [Mary Josephine Pratt](people/person_1205.qmd).
[^2]: Alice Julia Argles (b.1848/9) married (1880) [Willingham Franklin Rawnsley](people/person_1225.qmd), who ran a school at Lyndhurst.  His pupils would be Queen Victoria’s grandsons: Prince [Leopold](people/person_868.qmd) (1884–1954), second Duke of Albany and Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha;  and the sons of Princess Beatrice, Prince [Alexander](people/person_122.qmd) (1886-1960), Prince [Leopold Henry](people/person_123.qmd) (1889–1922) and Prince [Maurice](people/person_124.qmd) (1891-1914) of Battenberg.
[^3]: These stories were published in Maria Edgeworth, *Rosamond: A Sequel to Early Lessons* (London: Hunter and Baldwin 1821).
